cefrAlignment: Fits B2 (CEFR CV reading for information and argument: can scan longer texts to locate relevant details): three passages of 369–507 words on general-interest topics, with statements that paraphrase details and require checking both content and information type.
examFidelity: Mirrors IELTS Matching information (paragraph letters, details not main ideas, unused paragraphs, letters reusable when the NB says so); I solved all 28 items before reading the key, and after one fix every statement has exactly one defensible paragraph; tips no longer state as fact that a paragraph will be used twice.
fixes: ex2 item 1 ('what makes customers satisfied with a service') could also match paragraph C (customers leave pleased); reworded to 'a claim that the experience of waiting can matter more than the service itself' so only A fits
ex4 Q3 claimed the word 'energy' appears in paragraphs C and E, but it appears only in C; rewrote the item around 'electricity' (C, D and E) and updated the options and explanation
Softened the learn tip and the IELTS exam tip: 'you may use any letter more than once' means a paragraph may contain two answers, not that one is likely or expected (ielts.org does not say so)
learnerOutcome: A learner can identify what type of information a statement asks for, scan lettered paragraphs for its paraphrase, and reject paragraphs that only share the topic.
